title: Browser approval gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate machine_browser_approval approves the installer's Match code in the test machine's operator identity browser on Linux, WSL and macOS. The operator identity is the project's browser-control default_identity; a project without one refuses machine_operator_identity_undeclared and names the settings and authorize commands. The recipe exports the standard BROWSER variable as yoke browser open for that identity, so the installer's link opens in the identity's signed-in Chromium profile, which listens on a loopback DevTools port. The installer's link opener honors BROWSER on every platform. One driver serves all three systems: it runs the test machine's installed Yoke over SSH (the internal yoke browser devtools tabs ORIGIN and yoke browser devtools approve URLS_JSON LABEL), which reads every ~/.yoke-browser-identities/*/*/DevToolsActivePort, so the host needs no other interpreter. A missing or unreadable receipt from that command refuses with reason identity_browser_helper_unreadable, naming the installed Yoke path. Every driver shares one matcher: only the installer-opened tab on the declared origin with the displayed code, revalidated before Approve machine is pressed, and only a same-origin navigation away from it or the visible connected confirmation in that tab counts. Native Windows keeps its own route until follow-up item YOK-5408. On Linux the gate first starts the test user's XFCE desktop and runs the installer on it; the step always attaches a desktop screenshot. A host without a desktop refuses headless_linux_browser_approval_unavailable and names the provisioning recovery. A setup that exits before or during approval fails the gate as terminal_setup_exited with its exit code and printed refusal, not as missing approval context. When the driver does not confirm the approval, the gate fails at once as machine_browser_approval_not_confirmed instead of waiting out gate_timeout_seconds; the driver's own code stays in browser_automation_error_code with a recovery. While it waits, each heartbeat prints a machine_qa.heartbeat line (phase operator_gate) that yoke watch qa-plan counts as progress; starting-state reset, fixture cleanup and restore print the same line on a background heartbeat. Approval coordinates use the shared MATCH_CODE_ALPHABET, MATCH_CODE_LENGTH and derived MATCH_CODE_PATTERN exported by yoke_contracts.machine_authorization: exactly four characters from 23456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ. The complete verification URI must contain exactly the displayed match code on the declared HTTPS origin, or on a declared loopback HTTP origin (a case that prepares the admission fixture declares its own server, which is how company sign-in approves the teammate's machine). The gate sends at most Enter before approving; the agent-mode setup driver opens the link itself with --open-link. Other code formats, mismatched codes, duplicate query values and unrelated origins refuse before browser approval. The gate's machine_qa.operator_gate line carries self_approving true: yoke watch qa-plan counts it as progress, and the code needs no action and is never forwarded. Live proof on real hosts is still owed.
